# @moku-labs/editor

> Editor, devtools and MCP layer for @moku-labs/game, built on @moku-labs/core. Three Moku cores in one package: `editor-agent` on the game page, `editor-server` in Bun, `editor-tools` on the tools page. One registry of sources and commands feeds the in-game overlay, the tools page, MCP and headless tests. On a phone a debug build (`moku-game build --debug`) carries the same agent: the overlay's frame graph names each spike's cause, the recorder keeps a log on the device once someone records, and `moku-editor perf` on the computer pairs the phone, writes its logs and summarizes them. The tools page's Render workspace, Mission control, reads one source at a time: the local preview, or a phone connected from the editor by wire (Android, adb) or on the network; the local preview pauses while a phone is the source. The editor reaches the game only through `@moku-labs/game/inspect` and `@moku-labs/game/control` (plus the game's `.dev` modules). ESM only. Bun for the server; browser for the agent and the tools page.

- Package: `@moku-labs/editor` (MIT)
- Peer dependencies: `@moku-labs/game >= 0.15.0` and `typescript >= 5.5`, both required (the project index, `@moku-labs/game/project`, needs `typescript`; the engine page, `@moku-labs/game/cli` `preparePage` and `watchKeys`, needs game 0.13.1). The phone tools (perf, recorder, the overlay's frame graph, debug builds) need the engine release with the build flags, the renderer monitor (`app.renderer.monitor`) and the `debug` plugin (`app.debug.overlay`) (0.15.0, the peer floor). The pass owners, filters and draws, the `shader` and `problem` events, the sample's object counts and render targets, the app id and control on `--debug` builds need 0.15.1, the engine the editor is developed and tested against; on 0.15.0 those blocks are absent (read not measured) and `--debug` runs read and cosmetic commands only.
- Doors: element rects come from `game.locate { key }` when the manifest lists it (0.4), else `game.rect { key }` (0.1); neither listed: nothing is read and the picker says "This game reports no element rects". `game.capture` answers a PNG data URL (0.1) or `{ png, legend? }` (0.4); capture takes both. The contact sheet (`editor.sheet`, MCP `moku_series`) needs game 0.4.
- Runtime dependencies: `@moku-labs/core`, `@moku-labs/common`, `preact`, `elkjs`
- Bin, engine page (B5): `moku-editor [--root DIR] [--preload FILE]… [--serve-plugin FILE]…` with no html, in a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`): the bin imports `@moku-labs/game/cli` from the game root, calls `preparePage(root, { agents: ["@moku-labs/editor/agent/page"], preload, servePlugins })` (paths resolved against the cwd), starts the engine's keys watch `watchKeys(root, { onError })` from the same import (it resolves after the first scan, so `generated/` is fresh; a failed scan is one warning; the watch is closed when the child exits), and always re-runs itself as `bun --config=<root>/.moku/bunfig.toml <bin> <root>/.moku/index.html --root <root>` in the root (D-51), so Bun loads the engine's hot plugin. Not a moku-game folder: exit 2; the engine refuses: its `[game] …` message, exit 1. From an editor working tree the bin appends `<tree>/scripts/tree/bundle.ts` to the serve plugins (D-50): the page bundles the tree's `dist/` on the game's one engine copy. `--preload` and `--serve-plugin` with an html file, or on `mcp` / `mcp-config`, are errors.
- Bin, html: `moku-editor <game-html> [--port 3000] [--root .] [--no-hmr] [--help]` (Bun only). Serves with Bun hot reload on (D-23); `--no-hmr` starts it off, and the Hot reload switch flips it while the bin runs (D-32). Bun reads `[serve.static]` of `bunfig.toml` from the process cwd only, so when `--root` holds such a bunfig and the cwd is another folder the bin re-runs itself in the root: run it from anywhere. `moku-editor mcp [<game-html>] [--port N] [--root DIR] [--no-hmr]` is the stdio MCP server for Claude Code; `moku-editor mcp-config [<game-html>] [--port N]` prints its `.mcp.json` snippet and `claude mcp add` line.
- Bin, e2e (D-52, D-53): `moku-editor e2e -c <playwright config> [playwright args…]` runs a game's editor Playwright specs with one Playwright process, so one fresh editor bin, per project and spec file, because Bun's dev server degrades after many hot reloads in one process. One `--list --reporter=json` run with the user's words makes the plan (`--project`, files, `-g` narrow it); each (project, file) pair runs with `--project=<p>`, an anchored file regex and `--pass-with-no-tests` on its own `PORT` (`PORT`, else 4417, plus its index), without the user's `--project` and file words; `--reporter` skips the list, `--shard` / `--last-failed` act on the list only; `--project a b` is variadic as in Playwright, up to a path-like word (a `/`, or `.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.mjs` at the end), which is a file filter. A run holds `.moku/e2e.lock` (its pid) in the cwd: a second run while it lives exits 1 with "[moku-editor] another e2e run (pid N) holds .moku/e2e.lock: wait for it, or delete the file when no run is left"; a dead pid's lock is taken over; `--list` takes no lock. One line per run (`<project> · <file> · passed · 12.3 s`) and a summary (`e2e: <n> runs · <failed> failed · <s> s`). A failed run's line and a failing summary print as errors; a warning names the tests of an unnamed project that did not run. A `--list` or an empty plan runs once as given, `CI=true` installs Chromium first, exit = the first failing code.
- Bin, perf (device mode): `moku-editor perf [--lan] [--port 47600] [--out .moku/perf] [--every 10] [--no-ui]` starts the server core (files, hub, connect, collector, pages) without a game, turns on the hub's device listeners (`127.0.0.1:<port>` for adb reverse; with `--lan` the computer's LAN address, paired phones only), pairs phones (an adb phone at once under `pairing: "lan"`, a LAN phone by its four-digit code typed in the terminal), serves the tools page on the device port (`http://127.0.0.1:47600/__editor/#render`, Mission control with the phone as its source; device mode is perf's, so a LAN code is typed in the terminal; off with `--no-ui`), prints one live block per phone log and writes `.moku/perf/perf-<yyyymmdd>-<hhmm>-<model>.jsonl` (every line with `rx`). The switches map onto `hub.devicePort`, `hub.deviceLan`, `collector.out`, `collector.everyS`, `pages.toolsPage`. Ctrl+C: `hub.stopDevices()`, `collector.settled()`, `editor.stop()`, then a summary per log. `.moku/perf.json` (0600, holds the hub token) lets `moku-editor perf mark "<label>"` post a mark from a second terminal to the collector's token-protected route `{path}/perf/mark`. `moku-editor perf summary <log.jsonl>` prints one row per screen and rate (frames, p50/p90/p99, GPU, spikes by cause, passes, texture MB art/tgt/kept, heap), the rate switches, the screen events (pool trims, warm-ups, the game's overlays), heat, system frames, marks; `moku-editor perf compare <a.jsonl> <b.jsonl>` compares by screen and rate with ▲/▼ at ±10 %.
- Full reference: llms-full.txt (every Config, Api and event type verbatim). Both llms files ship in the package.
- Built for a narrow pane: Claude's browser pane at 1/3 (480 px) or 1/2 (720 px) of the screen; every workspace works at 480 px.

## Entry points

| Import | What |
|---|---|
| `@moku-labs/editor` | Runtime-free: wire protocol types and pure helpers (with `refusalOf`, `isAllowed` and the types `BuildInfo`, `BuildProfile`, `CommandRefusal`, `CommandVia`, `OverlayMarker`), `definePanel` and panel types. Imports no plugin and no core. `perf/protocol`, `perf/graph` and `collector/report` are not root exports: their types are `Perf.*` and `Collector.*`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/agent` | Agent core for the game page; defaults `registry`, `channel`, `perf`, `recorder`, `overlay`, opt-in `bridge`, `capture`. `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `bridgePlugin`, `capturePlugin`, `channelPlugin`, `overlayPlugin`, `perfPlugin`, `recorderPlugin`, `registryPlugin`; namespaces `Bridge`, `Capture`, `Channel`, `Overlay`, `Perf`, `Recorder`, `Registry`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/agent/page` | Default export only: the engine's `PageAgent` (D-49). The dev page (`moku-game dev`, the bin's engine page) and a debug build (`moku-game build --debug`, `native build --debug`) call it after the game started. Behind the inline guard `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__ \|\| __MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` it stops a previous `globalThis.editor`, starts the agent core with `bridgePlugin` and `capturePlugin` on `{ app, name, modules }` and sets `globalThis.editor`; with neither flag it starts nothing, and a release build drops the body. No side effect on import. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/server` | Server core for Bun; defaults `files`, `hub`, `connect`, `collector`, `pages`. `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `collectorPlugin`, `connectPlugin`, `filesPlugin`, `hubPlugin`, `pagesPlugin`; namespaces `Collector`, `Connect`, `Files`, `Hub`, `Pages`. |
| `@moku-labs/editor/tools` | Tools core for the tools page; defaults `link`, `activeSource`, `workspace`, `panels` and the six views. `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `linkPlugin`, `activeSourcePlugin`, `workspacePlugin`, `panelsPlugin`, `flowViewPlugin`, `gameViewPlugin`, `renderViewPlugin`, `stateViewPlugin`, `filesViewPlugin`, `consoleViewPlugin`; namespaces `Link`, `ActiveSource`, `Workspace`, `Panels`, `FlowView`, `GameView`, `RenderView`, `StateView`, `FilesView`, `ConsoleView`. |

## Core concepts

- Three cores (decision D-01): `src/config.ts` has three `createCoreConfig` calls, each with its own Config and global Events. Each runtime gets its own bundle: Bun code never reaches the browser, Preact never reaches the server.
- Every core registers the core plugins `logPlugin` and `envPlugin` from `@moku-labs/common`: `ctx.log` and `ctx.env` on every plugin.
- Global configs `AgentConfig`, `ServerConfig`, `ToolsConfig` are empty. Every option belongs to a plugin and is set through `pluginConfigs` (shallow merge; arrays replace).
- Registry: the doors and `.dev` modules become closure-erased entries. Raw `Json` in, `checkInput` against the descriptor's `InputSchema`, door call, `toWireValue` out.
- Manifest: descriptors only (`sources`, `commands`), plus `game`, `page`, `embedded`. Sent by the bridge in `hello`.
- Not installed: the registry probes every door source once with its default input at start and on each manifest rebuild (never `game.rect` or `game.locate`, which locate one element). A door that throws (a game without `effectsPlugin`, a screenless game without `ui`/`world`, game 0.4.2's `game.sounds` without `audioPlugin`: `[game] The source game.sounds needs audioPlugin.`) is listed with `available: false` and `reason`; its reads and watches answer -32008 `not_installed` (not retryable). The link neither logs nor retries it; Render reads "Effects not installed in this game".
- Production builds: import the agent only inside `if (__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) { await import("@moku-labs/editor/agent") }`. With the flag `false` the bundle keeps no editor code; the package is `"sideEffects": false` and the agent core and every agent plugin are `/* @__PURE__ */`. The dev agent (perf with Mission control's feeds, recorder, the overlay with its three subset Barlow faces, bridge, capture) is 299,859 B minified, 122,297 B gzip, bounded at 124 KB gzip (124,000 B, raised from 120 KB by the owner for Mission control's feeds) by `tests/integration/agent-bundle.test.ts`; the phone only reads, the tools page builds the marks, the pass chains and the history.
- Debug builds (engine spec 10): `moku-game build --debug` (DEV `false`, AGENT `true`, CONTROL `true` on engine 0.15.1: every command; `--debug=full` is its alias; on 0.15.0 `--debug` had CONTROL `false`) and `--debug=read` (CONTROL `false`: read and cosmetic commands run), `--editor host:port` (default `127.0.0.1:47600`, `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__`), `moku-game native build android --debug` (the debug app `<appId>.debug` beside the store app). The page agent runs behind the inline guard `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__ || __MOKU_GAME_AGENT__`: a debug build keeps it (299,807 B, 123,404 B gzip), a release build (both `false`) drops it (0 B of editor code; the entry is 155 B, 141 B gzip); the store check looks for `/__editor/hello` and `[moku-editor]`. `Manifest.build` is `{ profile: "dev" | "full" | "read" | "none", id?, engine?, appId? }`; each command descriptor carries `allowed` (and `reason` `"read-only"` / `"dev-only"` when refused) and the game's `overlay` marker; a refused run answers -32009 (`read_only` / `dev_only`).
- The overlay (agent default): hidden, pill or card (tabs Frames, Game, Record, Link). The game opens it through the engine's `debug` plugin (`app.debug.overlay.open({ mode })` / `close` / `toggle` / `isOpen`, `DebugTrigger()`, `config.debug.overlay` applied by `startPage` after the agents), which reaches `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__`; the editor ships no gesture and no debug button. The Game tab lists only the commands the game marked `overlay: "toggle" | "button"`; a read-only build greys the rest ("needs a debug build of a newer engine, or without --debug=read"). The Record tab is `OFF` until someone records and says who started a log. The overlay emits `overlay:changed` (the recorder logs it as the `devtools` event; `overlay` is the game's event) and `overlay:connect` (the bridge dials it).
- Device session: a phone linked to the hub's device listener (`kind=agent role=device`), paired at once by wire or by a four-digit code on the network; an ordinary agent session that every tools page sees, with `SessionInfo.device` `{ id, model, link: "adb" | "lan", address, port, engine, build, appId? }`. Device mode starts from `moku-editor perf` or from the dev tools page (the server's `connect`: Render's Connect panel, `connect.wire` / `connect.network`). No iOS debug build exists yet: an iPhone cannot link.
- One active source (tools `activeSource`): the page reads the local preview (its own game frame) or one phone or another page, never a mix. A switch to a phone pauses the local preview first (`game.pause` through `link.runIn`; a game the person paused stays theirs) and going back resumes it; a phone that links becomes the source (`autoUse`); a phone that leaves returns the page to the local preview with a notice and a timeline marker, and is the source again when it rejoins within 15 s. The top bar's source pill, the disconnect notice and the paused veil show it; the Game workspace reads no scene from a phone.
- Mission control (Render): the connection bar, a 2-minute frame timeline kept on the tools page (GC lane, rate, shader, recording and source-switch marks, a Shaders & passes lane, pause/rewind/step, range selection with an inspector), the cards (FPS with the rate switch, frame time, draws, textures, GPU passes, memory, device load), Record and Monitoring, and collapsed Scene details. Fed by perf's `editor.perf.second`, `editor.perf.frames { after }`, `editor.perf.events { after }`, `editor.perf.passes`, `editor.perf.detail { from, to }`, the command `editor.perf.sections`, and `editor.recorder`. Not measured is never 0.
- Memory sources: a phone's JS heap comes from CDP over USB (connect attaches `Runtime.getHeapUsage` through `adb forward`); an Android WebView's `performance.memory` is frozen (10.68 MB on a Galaxy A26 while the heap swings 27–57 MB) and never shown as the phone's heap; a phone on the network reads "Not available: connect by wire to read the heap". Wired telemetry (GPU clock and busy %, CPU and memory per process, JS heap and inferred GCs) is published as `editor.deviceTelemetry` once a second and logged by the collector as `telemetry` lines while the phone records.
- Recording: off by default (`recorder.autoStart: false`). The overlay's Record tab, Render's Record and an agent (`editor.record { on?, label?, mark? }` → `{ on, file, startedBy, marked }`, MCP door tool `editor_record`) start, stop and mark the same log; `startedBy` is `{ by: "phone" | "editor" | "agent" | "remote" | "code" | "auto", name }` (the hub stamps an MCP client's name on its runs). Engine fingerprint: `files.engine()` (`EngineInfo` `{ id, version, dist, patch? }`) is published as `editor.engine`; `link.engine()` reads it; the overlay and the strip show STALE when the phone's `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` differs.
- Scenarios (dev only): the engine dev page starts from `tests/scenarios/<name>.ts` when its URL carries `?player=<name>`; `link.frameUrl(url, { player })` tags it, `workspace.scenarios()` / `setScenario(name)` drive the picker. A debug build carries no scenarios.
- EditorChannel: `read`, `watch`, `run`, `status`. In process it is the agent `channel`; remote it is the tools `link`. Every panel reads through it.
- Source `changes`: `frame` (re-read by the bridge once per heartbeat), `commit`, `edge` (followed by watch). Values are sent only when their JSON text changed.
- Command `effect`: `read`, `route`, `cosmetic`, `cheat`, `raw`. Editor-owned commands (`editor.*`) cannot be `cheat` or `raw`.
- Sessions: one per connected game page, id `s-` + 4 hex. Tools pick one: sticky choice, then this tab's own game frame (`__editorFrame`), then newest embedded, then newest. activeSource is the only plugin that changes the choice for a source switch (a phone or back to the local preview).
- Heartbeat: `{ frame, paused, at, heap? }`; `heap { usedMb, limitMb }` only in Chromium. Taps: the bridge sends `tap { x, y, at }` per pointerdown (at most one per 50 ms); `link.onTap` gets them; workspace draws ripples.
- Tools page: Game is the default workspace; ⌘1–⌘6 = Game, Flow, Render, State, Files, Console. Density `auto` (compact below 820 px) / `compact` / `comfortable`. The element picker (the Select button of the Game toolbar, ⇧⌘C or I) is the one way to pick: the cursor over the game is a crosshair, a click picks one element and a drag of 4 px or more picks an area (`area-f<frame>.md`: the elements fully inside, else the ones covered by half; group roots, top to bottom, at most 40; each with its child tree (two spaces per level, 3 levels, 60 lines), `text "…"` when the game reports one and `x,y w×h px` bounds; one `layout:` line per parent chain, `partly in the area:` (at most 8) and `## <key> · component <Name> · <file:line>` for each component used). The pinned preview plays the game; S/M/L sizes it. Views' side panels are one `SidePanel` (resize, collapse, close, reopen, overlay drawer).
- Top bar (round 2, 2b R15): it starts with the game mark `span[data-mark]`, the initials of the game name on a 24 px tile coloured from the name (`TT` for "Tic Tac Toe", `ME` for "Merge", `·` on a neutral tile without a game; the same name always gets the same hue). From 900 px it shows the source pill (the page's one source: "Local preview", "Galaxy A26 · by wire"; its menu holds Local preview, the linked phones and Connect device…), the Preview (G), Overlay (O) and Hot reload (H) switches with labels, Registry (icon; counts in its title) and theme. Below 900 px it is compact: the game mark, game name, link pill (session in its title), Pause and Step as icons (labels are their accessible names), the Hot reload icon toggle (flame with a dot while on, `aria-pressed`, H), a search icon and a ⋯ menu (`data-action="more"`) holding Game preview, Overlay in game, Hot reload (each with its state and its key), Registry, Density and Theme. At 560 px and narrower the game name goes; Hot reload is the one icon toggle at every compact width. The icon shares the `data-action` of its menu row: `[data-ui=top-bar] > [data-action=hot-reload]`, `[data-ui=more-menu] [data-action=hot-reload]`.
- Copy on select (D-68, D-70, D-72): the preference "Copy reference on select" (`workspace.copyOnSelect()`, `setCopyOnSelect(on)`; persisted, on by default; no key). Its control is the "Copy Ref" switch of the Game toolbar (`[data-game=toolbar] [data-part=copy-on-select]`, `role="switch"`, after Safe area and Sound; title "On: a pick writes the reference and copies its line. Off: a pick only selects the element"); a palette command flips it too. The top bar has no control for it. On: a picker click writes the reference (bookmark, crop, full frame, card) and copies its line. Off: a picker click only selects the element for the Element tab and publishes the selection without `card`, `crop` and `line`; no bookmark, no capture, no file, no capture card, no toast, no clipboard; an area drag picks nothing. "Copy reference" in the Element tab always writes the card and copies its line. MCP `moku_select` does not ask the preference.
- Pick for the chat (round 2, 2b R13): a picker click bookmarks the game (`gameView.bookmarks()`), saves `<day>/<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg` (the element + 8 px) and `<day>/f<frame>-full.jpg` (the frame; JPEG 0.8 by default, D-34), writes the card `<day>/<key>-f<frame>.md` (`-2` … when taken that day); `<day>` is today's folder `<capturesDir>/<yyyy-mm-dd>` (local date), where Shot (`<hhmm>-<flow>.jpg`) and Series (`series-<hhmm>/`) write too; old flat files stay and puts ONE line on the clipboard. All of this only while "Copy reference on select" is on (the Copy Ref switch of the Game toolbar); with it off the click only selects the element. "Copy reference" in the footer of the Element tab writes the card of the selection again and copies its line (`copyReference()` returns it):

  ```text
  @moku settingsBoard panel · settingsPopup/open · features/settings/settings.tsx:290 · ref 65,641 950×1060 · .moku/captures/2026-10-05/settingsBoard-f212.md
  ```

  Line fields: name and type, flow/node, the `file:line` of the key (an entity: the line that defines its projection), `ref` bounds in the game's reference units, the card path; an unknown field is left out. The card is Markdown: `# @moku <name> <type>`, the full reference block in a `text` fence, `## JSX · <file:line>` and `## Style · <name> · <file:line>` fenced snippets (an entity: `## Spawned by <projection> · <file:line>` and its components), then `![element](<key>-f<frame>-crop.jpg)` and `![frame](f<frame>-full.jpg)`. The block in the card:

  ```text
  @moku settingsBoard · panel · settingsPopup/open · f212
  path: settingsScreen/settingsBoard
  source: features/settings/settings.tsx:290 · texture: ui.panel-signboard
  layout: settingsScreen (column, padding 0/0/0/0)
  bounds: 24,233 346×386 px · ref 65,641 950×1060
  state: visible
  flow: board > settings > open · last: board/settings/enter → done
  game: merge-game 0.0.0 · s-1f12 · f212 · 15:31:13 · live · clean
  device: iPhone 15 393×852 portrait · dpr 3 · safe 59/0/34/0
  restore: bookmark settingsBoard-f210
  shot: .moku/captures/2026-10-05/settingsBoard-f212-crop.jpg · frame: .moku/captures/2026-10-05/f212-full.jpg
  ```

  An unknown line or field is left out. `bounds` is device px, then the game's reference units (`SceneNode.refRect`). `restore` names the kept bookmark: `panels.run("game.restore", { bookmark: gameView.bookmarks()[0].value })` goes back to it.
- Devices (round 2b R9, R10): twenty-one presets grouped iPhone (SE 3 · small, 2022 with the home-button frame, 15, 17e approx, Air approx, 18 Pro approx — the default, 18 Pro Max approx, then 15 Pro Max, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max), Android (Galaxy S24, Galaxy A55, Redmi Note 13 approx, Pixel 8, Xperia 1 V 21:9), Foldable (Galaxy Z Fold 6 approx, Galaxy Z Flip 6, Pixel 9 Pro Fold approx, iPhone Duo approx: cover 466×678, inner 890×626 landscape-wide; the folding ones with Fold/Unfold), Tablet (iPad mini 7, iPad Air 11"), Desktop. Each has `dpr`, safe insets (Android, foldable and tablet report 0), a screen `radius` and `frame` (`"modern"` | `"home-button"`); the docked frame is clipped round. Fit is one scale per kind (the tallest preset of the kind, bezel included), so an SE shows smaller than an 18 Pro Max; foldables are phones; 100 % is 1 CSS px per px.
- Game toolbar (round 2b): its switches are Safe area, Sound and Copy Ref (the "Copy reference on select" preference, see above). A Sound switch (key M in Game) runs `game.mute { muted }` when the manifest lists it and keeps the flag (`workspace.muted()`, `setMuted(on)`, re-applied to every game that connects); without `game.mute` (game before 0.4.4) it is dimmed, title "Needs @moku-labs/game with game.mute". Select (`button[data-part="pick"]`, title "Select element ⇧⌘C") is an icon button, lit (`aria-pressed`) from the click until the pick completes, Esc or a second click. The Element tab's Code section (`data-part="code"`) shows the picked element's JSX and its `defineStyle` block with `file:line`, Open in Files and highlighting (20 lines, then "Show all N lines"); an entity shows "Spawned by <projection> · <file:line>" and its components. The capture card (Shot, pick, Series) is compact: a 56 px thumbnail, one line each for the title, the path (cut in the middle, the whole path in `title`) and `f<frame> · <device>`, then Copy link, Open and (a pick) Reference; at most 360 × 120 px. A series ends like a Shot (D-69): the capture card of its first shot, `series: <folder> (<n> frames)` on the clipboard and the toast "✓ N shots saved". The contact sheet of a series opens only on request: "Open contact sheet" in Files, Open on the series card, or `openSheet(indexPath)`.
- Element tab and pending style edits (D-67): the tab has no reference text block and no "Pick another"; its footer has "Copy reference" and "Show in render tree". The Styles rows are fields: a number, a text or a checkbox per value, one field per leaf of a record (`padding.top`). A change is recorded as a pending edit (`gameView.editStyle(path, to)`), not applied: the editor writes no file and sends no command, and the game does not change until the source is edited. An edited row shows the scene value struck through and a reset ×. Under the rows the edits bar says "N edits · M elements" with "Copy for agent" and "Clear" (`clearEdits("all")`). "Copy for agent" (`copyEdits()`) puts a text block on the clipboard, one block per element, the selected one first:

  ```text
  @moku homePlay · features/stage/views/home-screen.tsx:199
  minWidth: 556 -> 600
  padding.top: 25 -> 30
  ```

  The edits of the selected element also go out as `SelectionInfo.edits` (`StyleEdit` = `{ path, from, to }`, `StyleValue` = `number | string | boolean`), so MCP `moku_selection` answers them. An edit leaves by itself when a scene snapshot shows its `to` value: the agent wrote the code and hot reload brought it in. A new game session drops the edits of elements without a ui key; a page load drops all of them.
- Text style section of the Element tab (D-73): the engine sends the text style key a `text` was given (`UiNode.textStyle`, @moku-labs/game 0.14.11; the peer range is unchanged, an older game shows no section), and the scene keeps it as `SceneNode.textStyle` (a non-empty string, else dropped). For such a node the tab shows `section[data-part="text-style"]`, titled "Text style · <key>", inside the Styles section above the edits bar: `<path>:<line>` of the key's block with "Open in Files", then one row per field of the block. The block is the project index's answer for `textStyle:<key>`, parsed by the shared style edit (`parseStyleFile`, `findBlock`, kind `text`). A number literal and a quoted string are fields like the Styles rows (Enter or blur commits, Esc restores, `data-edited`, the file value struck, a reset ×); any other value (`colors.cream`, an identifier, a boolean, a call) is read-only text. A key the index does not know shows `Not in the project index: textStyle:<key>` and no fields. An edit is a pending edit of the STYLE KEY, not of the node: `state.edits` keeps it under `textStyle:<key>` with `label` `textStyle <key>`, `source` the block's path and line, `byId: false`; `from` is the value in the file; every text node with the key shows it. It resolves when the block, read again (on selection and on a `link:project` change that touches its file), has the `to` value; a field that is no number or quoted string any more in a block that was read drops its edit, another value in the file becomes the `from` of the edit, and a block that cannot be read keeps the edits. The edits bar counts it, `clearEdits("selected")` on a text node drops its own edits and the ones of its key, and the agent text gets one block per style key after the element blocks:

  ```text
  @moku textStyle ui.button · shared/styles/text.ts:88
  size: 105 -> 96
  ```

  `SelectionInfo.edits` of a selected text node also carries the edits of its style key, each with the path `textStyle:<key>#<field>` (`textStyle:ui.button#size`, `textStyle:ui.button#shadow.dy`). The `#` ends the key: a key and a field both have dots. The "Style · <key>" line and the Code section's text style snippet use `SceneNode.textStyle` when the JSX lookup of the node gave no text style (a key built in code).
- LinkStatus: `connecting`, `live { frame }`, `paused { frame }`, `silent { since, lastFrame }`, `lost { reason, lastFrame, retryInMs }`, `empty`.
- Panels are data (D-04): `definePanel` returns a frozen spec; the `panels` host owns subscriptions, first-value waiting, stale marking, teardown.
- Views never depend on each other (D-13): cross-view intents are global tools events (`workspace:open-file`, `workspace:select-node`, …).
- One game iframe (D-14): `workspace` owns it and never moves it in the DOM; views dock it and draw in its overlay.
- Live edits (D-07, D-23): with Bun hot reload on (the bin's default) a save of a game source makes Bun reload the game page; the bridge stores a `game.bookmark` checkpoint in `sessionStorage` before and restores it after (hello `manifest.restored`), toast "Game reloaded · state restored". Without it (`--no-hmr`, a game's own server, or no new page within `hotReloadWaitMs`) the editor runs D-07: `game.bookmark` → reload the frame → `game.restore` on reconnect. The session reads tainted. The Hot reload switch (key H) turns it off and on while the bin runs (D-32): Bun cannot change HMR on a running server, so the bin restarts its server with HMR flipped on the same port (token kept, every socket drops for about a second), and the tools page reloads the game frame with its checkpoint, so the page gains or drops `/_bun/client`; toasts "Hot reload off" / "Hot reload on", then "Game reloaded · state restored from the last checkpoint". While off, a save on disk does not reload the game. A game's own server owns it (the switch is inert); a failed switch says to restart the bin with or without `--no-hmr`. Measured on merge-game (e2e/edit-loop.spec.ts): save → updated frame in about 30 ms with the hot swap (a recolour, read back from captured frames, about 0.1 s); a reload with the state restored takes about 0.8 s. Hot swap (game 0.5.0): with `[serve.static] plugins = ["@moku-labs/game/hot"]` in the game root's `bunfig.toml`, a save of a view module (`.tsx`, `styles.ts`, `view.ts`, `animations.ts`, `effects.ts`, generated strings, and since game 0.9.0 a `.ts` directly in `styles/`, `motion/`, `effects/`, `views/`, `world/projections/` or `world/layout/`) swaps in place: same session, no reload, toast "Game updated", and `gameFrame().reload()` resolves `{ restored: false, reason: "hot_swap" }` (it ends on the game's `ui:hot-swap` log entry). A logic module still reloads and restores, also under a popup.
- Only the game reloads (U9): during an expected reload (`link.expectReload()`, close 1012, a game's bye; `isReloading(status)`) the top bar keeps its name, session and pill width, the panels keep their data, and one spinner `[data-frame-reloading]` shows on the game frame. A real loss, or one past link's `reloadGraceMs` (8000), shows the red bar over the workspace, never in the flow.
- Project index (D-38 … D-48): `files` opens the project index of its root on start (`@moku-labs/game/project`); the tools page asks it through `link.files.find(key)` and reads the key maps from `link.project()` (`link:project` with a `ProjectDelta`). It is the only source of code locations (node and flow files, Code tab, Used by, the picked element's JSX and style, projections, text styles, the asset manifest). Index off: one line `Project index is off: <reason>` in every view that needs a location (log `files:project-off` at error); a key it does not know: `Not in the project index: <key>`. No `bunfig.toml` needed for it. Removed: the node → file rule (`nodeFile`, `flowFile`, kebab), crawls, `.moku/editor/files.json`, configs `flowView.stylesFile`, `gameView.manifestPaths`, `gameView.sourceSearch`, `renderView.manifestPaths`. A versioned write checks the version right before the rename (window narrowed, not closed).
- Files sandbox (D-09): `files` works under one root, allowlist + denylist, realpath check, atomic writes, optional sha1 `version`.
- Security: the server binds 127.0.0.1 only; Host, Origin and a per-start 43-char token gate every upgrade. The token is never logged or printed. Device mode (`moku-editor perf`, or the tools page through connect) adds `127.0.0.1:47600` and, on request (`--lan`, On the network), a LAN listener for paired phones' sockets only (device Origins, pairing confirmed by the person in the terminal or the tools page, a per-device token); the server spawns `adb` only while device mode runs or the Connect panel lists phones; connect's `connect.*` editor methods reach tools sockets only, and its CDP client sends an allowlist of read methods over a loopback `adb forward`.
- Tools page ships prebuilt (D-06): `bun run build:tools` bundles `src/plugins/pages/page/` into `dist/tools/`; `pages` serves it.

## Quick start

Game page (dev entry; the agent drops out of a production build):

```ts
if (__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) {
  const { bridgePlugin, capturePlugin, createApp } = await import("@moku-labs/editor/agent");
  const editor = createApp({
    plugins: [bridgePlugin, capturePlugin],
    pluginConfigs: { registry: { game: app, modules: [mergeDev], name: "merge-game 0.0.0" } }
  });
  await editor.start(); // after the game; never waits for the editor server
}
```

Server (Bun):

```ts
import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/editor/server";
import index from "./index.html";

const editor = createApp({ pluginConfigs: { files: { root: `${import.meta.dir}/..` } } });
await editor.start();
Bun.serve(editor.hub.serve({ port: 3000, routes: { "/": index }, fetch: serveAsset }));
// tools page: http://127.0.0.1:3000/__editor/
```

Or the bin: `bunx moku-editor --root .` in a moku-game folder (the engine writes the page with the editor's agent), or `bunx moku-editor web/index.html --port 3000 --root .` for a game HTML file.

Tools page (what the prebuilt page does):

```ts
import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/editor/tools";

const tools = createApp({});
await tools.start();
tools.workspace.mount(document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("[data-editor-root]")!);
```

## Quick API reference

### Framework (each entry)

```ts
createApp(options?: { plugins?: Plugin[]; pluginConfigs?: { [plugin]: Partial<Config> } }): App
createPlugin(name: string, spec: { depends?, config?, createState?, api?, hooks?, onInit?, onStart?, onStop? }): Plugin
app.start(): Promise<void>
app.stop(): Promise<void>
app.<pluginName>        // the plugin api, e.g. app.hub, app.link, app.flowView
ctx.require(plugin)     // the api from inside another plugin
```

### Root (`@moku-labs/editor`)

```ts
definePanel(input: PanelInput<S, C>): PanelSpec
checkInput(schema: InputSchema, raw: Json): InputOf<schema>     // throws -32602
toWireValue(value: unknown): Json                               // $map, $set, $error tags; throws -32006
encode(message: Message): string
decode(text: string): Message
request(id, channel, method, params?, session?) / notification(...) / success(id, result) / failure(id, error)
isRequest / isResponse / isNotification / isFailure / isJson
wireError(code: number, message: string, data?: WireErrorData): Error & WireError
isWireError(value): value is WireError
toWireError(error: unknown): WireError
fromWireError(error: WireError): ProtocolError
isRetryable(error: unknown): boolean
bareMessage(message: string): string                            // strips "[moku-editor] "
isReloading(status: LinkStatus): boolean                        // a lost with reloading: true (an expected reload, U7/U9)
isHotSwapEntry(entry: Json): boolean                            // a game.log entry of an applied dev hot swap (ui:hot-swap, game 0.5.0)
errorCode, ERROR_PREFIX, ProtocolError                         // errorCode.notInstalled = -32008
parseProjectState(value) / parseFoundList(value)                // checked copies of editor.project and a find answer; undefined when bad
projectDelta(held, next): ProjectDelta                          // { all, files, moved, removed }: all after a revision gap, first state or off
firstDefinition(state, key): string | undefined                 // the first def path of a key: firstDefinition(link.project(), "node:board/merge")
anchorKey(ref, path): string                                    // the style: / textStyle: key of a style block
// types: ProjectState (off { reason } | on { revision, previous?, manifest?, defs, uses, broken, change? }), ProjectFound
// (path, binding?, key?, component?, kind?, stem?, prop?, line, range, hash, broken?), ProjectAnchor, ProjectDelta, ProjectChange, ProjectMove, FindParams
isSelectionInfo(value) / parseSelectionInfo(value) / parseSelectParams(value)     // SelectionInfo guard and checked copies
// types: StyleEdit ({ path, from, to }), StyleValue (number | string | boolean): SelectionInfo.edits, the pending style edits of the selected element; an edit of a text node's style key has the path `textStyle:<key>#<field>`
```

### Agent APIs

```ts
registry.manifest(): Manifest                    // probes door sources on each build; unavailable ones carry available: false

registry.game(): GameLike                        // the game app the registry serves
registry.build(): BuildInfo                      // { profile: "dev" | "full" | "read" | "none", id?, engine?, appId? }, read once
// registry's per-plugin event registry:command { id, input, via: "overlay" | "tools" | "mcp" | "bridge" | "local", ok }: every command run, with who ran it

channel.read(id: string, input?: Json): Promise<Json>
channel.watch(id: string, input: Json | undefined, onValue: (value: Json) => void): () => void

perf.spike(frame: number): PerfSpikeRecord | undefined                    // ring numbers, rate switch, the game's frame events, the spike line as detail
perf.monitor(): MonitorLike | undefined          // for the recorder; undefined while off
// sources editor.perf.second, editor.perf.window (PerfWindowWire), editor.perf.spikes, editor.perf.spike { frame }, editor.spikes { lastMs? }
// Mission control's feeds: editor.perf.frames { after? } (PerfFramesWire, hole: true when after left the window), editor.perf.events { after? } (PerfEventsWire),
// editor.perf.passes (PerfPassesWire), editor.perf.detail { from, to } (PerfDetailWire); command editor.perf.sections { gpu?, passes?, shaders?, problems?, memory?, systems?, nodes?, longFrames? } → PerfMonitorState

recorder.start(options?: { label?: string; by?: RecordStarter; name?: string }): LogFileInfo   // throws without a monitor; a running log is answered with its startedBy unchanged
recorder.stop(): Promise<LogFileInfo | undefined>
recorder.mark(label: string): boolean            // true when a log records
recorder.command(id: string, input: Json, label: string): boolean   // the overlay's automatic mark of a command it ran
recorder.status(): RecorderStatus                // { state, lines, bytes, sent, pending, monitor, file, label, sinceMs, storage, dropped, startedBy }
recorder.marks() / files(): copies
recorder.share(name: string): Promise<"shared" | "cancelled" | "downloaded">   // a log over 32 MiB is refused for the native share
recorder.remove(name: string): Promise<void>
recorder.unsentRun(max: number): { log, from, lines } | undefined   // the bridge's peek at the outbox
recorder.ack(log: string, next: number): void
// commands editor.record { on?, label?, mark? } → { on, file, startedBy, marked }, editor.mark { label }; source editor.recorder (status + the last 32 marks); per-plugin event recorder:status
// autoStart is false: nothing records until the phone, the tools page or an agent starts it

overlay.open(options?: { mode?: "pill" | "card"; tab?: OverlayTab }): void   // the card by default
overlay.close(): void
overlay.toggle(): void                           // hidden ↔ the last visible mode
overlay.isOpen(): boolean                        // pill or card
overlay.mode(): "hidden" | "pill" | "card"
overlay.commands(): readonly OverlayCommand[]    // the game's overlay: "toggle" | "button" commands, with allowed and reason
// command editor.overlay { mode: "hidden" | "pill" | "card" } → { mode }; global globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__ { open, close, toggle, isOpen }

bridge.status(): LinkStatus
bridge.session(): string | undefined
bridge.link(): DeviceLink | undefined            // device mode: { mode: "none" | "connecting" | "adb" | "lan", address, pairing?: { code }, editorEngine?, seenAt? }
bridge.connect(address: string): void            // switches to device mode at host:port; a bad address throws a TypeError
```

// connect.watch { device } → { wired, reason? }, connect.unwatch { device }; publishes editor.devices and editor.deviceTelemetry; per-plugin event connect:telemetry

## Global events

Declared in `src/config.ts`. An event is global only when its listener cannot depend on its emitter (a cycle, or the opt-in bridge); every other event is per-plugin (below).

```ts
type AgentEvents = {
  "bridge:status": { status: LinkStatus; session?: string; link?: DeviceLink };   // link in device mode only; hooked by overlay
  "overlay:changed": OverlayChanged;   // { mode: "hidden" | "pill" | "card"; tab }; hooked by recorder (the devtools log event)
  "overlay:connect": { address: string };   // the Link tab; hooked by the opt-in bridge
};
type ServerEvents = {
  "hub:session": HubSession;       // { id, game, open, reason?: "bye" | "game_reloaded" }
  "files:written": FilesWritten;   // { path, bytes, kind: "code" | "style" | "layout" | "capture" | "other" }
  "files:project": ProjectState;   // the project index opened, changed (a watch batch) or went off
};
type ToolsEvents = {
  "link:status": { status: LinkStatus; session?: string };
  "link:project": { state: ProjectState; delta: ProjectDelta };   // a new editor.project state; views drop what delta names
  "workspace:changed": { ws: WorkspaceId };
  "workspace:ran": RanEvent;
  "workspace:density": { density: "compact" | "comfortable" };
  "workspace:open-file": { path: string; line?: number };
  "workspace:select-node": { id: string };
  "workspace:focus-frame": { frame: number };
  "workspace:reveal": { ref: ElementRef };
  "workspace:inspect": { ref: ElementRef };
  "workspace:open-sheet": { index: string };
};
```

Per-plugin events, declared by their emitter with `register<T>()` and hooked only by plugins that list the emitter in `depends`:

```ts
"registry:command": RegistryCommandEvent;     // registry → recorder: { id, input, via: "overlay" | "tools" | "mcp" | "bridge" | "local", ok }, every command run
"recorder:status": RecorderStatusEvent;       // recorder → overlay, bridge: { state, lines, bytes, sent, pending }
"hub:device": HubDeviceEvent;                 // hub → collector, connect: listening | connected | lines | closed | stopped
"connect:telemetry": DeviceTelemetry;         // connect → collector: one record a second of a watched wired phone (a telemetry line while it records)
"collector:session": CollectorSessionEvent;   // collector → pages: { device, file, state, lines, lost, last }
"activeSource:changed": SourceChange;         // activeSource → workspace, renderView: { from, to, reason, at }
"activeSource:connect-requested": ConnectRequest;   // activeSource → renderView: { tab: "wire" | "network" | undefined }
```

## Plugins (22)

One line each: core · tier · purpose · key methods · events (E = emits, H = hooks).

### Agent core (`editor-agent`)

- registry · agent · Complex · wraps game doors, `.dev` modules and `editor.*` commands into entries; builds the Manifest with the page's `build` (with `appId`) and each command's `allowed` / `reason` / `overlay`; probes door sources (not installed → `available: false`, -32008); refuses what the build refuses (-32009); owns `./protocol` · `manifest`, `source`, `command`, `add`, `envelope`, `clock`, `game`, `build` · E `registry:command` (per-plugin)
- channel · agent · Standard · in-process EditorChannel: immediate read on watch, run in a microtask, timer heartbeat (default 1000 ms, `heap` in Chromium) · `read`, `watch`, `run`, `status`, `heartbeat`, `onHeartbeat` · no events
- perf · agent · Complex · the performance read model: reads the engine monitor's frame ring at 4 Hz into a 6 s window, ranks spike causes (gpu › upload › compile › longFrame › js › gc? › gap), keeps the newest log lines; off with its reason without a monitor; adds the sources `editor.perf.second`, `editor.perf.window`, `editor.perf.spikes`, `editor.perf.spike`, `editor.spikes` and Mission control's feeds `editor.perf.frames`, `editor.perf.events`, `editor.perf.passes`, `editor.perf.detail` and the command `editor.perf.sections` (the phone only reads; the tools page builds marks, pass chains and the history); houses the runtime-free `perf/protocol` (with the tools page's 2-minute history) and `perf/graph` · `status`, `readWindow`, `second`, `spikes`, `spike`, `monitor` · no events
- recorder · agent · Complex · the performance log on the device, off until the phone, the tools page or an agent starts it (`startedBy`), rotated at 32 MB: every monitor line for hours, serialized on its own timer, OPFS chunks or memory, share (a log over 32 MiB is refused for the native share), an outbox the bridge pulls; writes the editor's `devtools`, `command` and `recorder` monitor events; adds `editor.record { on?, label?, mark? }`, `editor.mark`, source `editor.recorder` (with the last 32 marks) · `start`, `stop`, `mark`, `command`, `status`, `marks`, `files`, `share`, `remove`, `unsentRun`, `ack` · E `recorder:status` (per-plugin); H `overlay:changed`, `registry:command`
- overlay · agent · Complex · the editor's window over the game: hidden, pill or card (Frames graph and counters, Game commands the game marked, Record, Link), docked and dragged inside the safe area, all work in the engine's agent bracket; sets `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__` for `app.debug.overlay`; adds command `editor.overlay { mode }` · `open`, `close`, `toggle`, `isOpen`, `mode`, `commands` · E `overlay:changed`, `overlay:connect`; H `bridge:status`, `recorder:status`
- bridge · agent · Complex · opt-in websocket to the hub: hello, requests, throttled values, taps (≤ 1 per 50 ms), backoff 1 s → 30 s, a checkpoint in sessionStorage across Bun's reload; hello `caps: ["run-from"]`, so each hub `run` carries who sent it (`via` tools or mcp, the MCP client's name); device mode on a phone: dials the device listener, pairs by a four-digit code (with the build's app id), re-pairs after a 4401 `unpaired`, ships the recorder's log as `perf.lines` with an ack; adds commands `editor.reload { restore? }` (checkpoint, then `location.reload()`) and `editor.clock` · `status`, `session`, `link`, `connect` · E `bridge:status`; H `overlay:connect`, `recorder:status`
- capture · agent · Standard · opt-in; adds `editor.capture { maxWidth?, key?, rect?, format?, quality? }` (JPEG 0.8 by default; `key` or `rect` crops plus 8 px), `editor.series`, `editor.seriesStop`, `editor.sheet { frames, everyMs, maxWidth?, format?, quality? }` (one `game.capture { sheet }`, game ≥ 0.4); `maxWidth` (64–4096) shrinks the picture in the page; never captures on its own; takes `game.capture` as a data URL (game 0.1) or `{ png }` (game 0.4) · no app api · no events

### Server core (`editor-server`)

- files · server · Standard · project-root sandbox: list, read, atomic write with sha1 version, image captures under `.moku/captures/`, the project index of the root (opened on start, kept fresh by its watch), the computer's engine fingerprint · `list`, `read`, `write`, `writeBinary`, `readBinary`, `resolve`, `root`, `find`, `project`, `engine`, `refreshEngine` · E `files:written`, `files:project`
- hub · server · Complex · websocket switchboard: guard, token, sessions (with the `heartbeat { frame, paused, silent }` readout), routing of `game` and `files` channels, shared watches, heartbeat and tap fan-out, backpressure, the `hotReload` notification, the editor page's `selection` (kept, replayed) and the `editor.select` relay to the page (`role=page`, D-33); wraps `Bun.serve`; publishes `editor.engine`; device mode: the adb and LAN device listeners (the LAN one on and off while it runs), pairing, a ping per phone (`latencyMs`), `perf.lines` / `perf.ack`, 4401 `unpaired` for a stale token, the runtime-free `hub/protocol`; run stamping (`from`, `client`); other plugins' editor methods for tools sockets only · `serve`, `token`, `sessions`, `fetch`, `websocket`, `addRoutes`, `guard`, `publish`, `closeAll`, `path`, `listenDevices`, `stopDevices`, `devices`, `listenLan`, `stopLan`, `addEditorMethods` · E `hub:session`, `hub:device` (per-plugin); H `files:project` (published as `editor.project`)
- connect · server · Complex · connect a phone from the tools page: device mode on and off on request, the device directory (`editor.devices`: phones adb lists, pairings asking, linked devices), the pairing confirm in the page, a phone matched by model and app id, and for a phone by wire CDP over `adb forward` and the wired telemetry (`editor.deviceTelemetry`, 1 Hz: GPU, CPU and memory per process, JS heap, inferred GCs); an adb allowlist and a CDP method allowlist; houses the runtime-free `connect/protocol` · `directory`, `telemetry`; editor methods `connect.scan`, `connect.wire`, `connect.network`, `connect.off`, `connect.confirm`, `connect.refuse`, `connect.watch`, `connect.unwatch` · E `connect:telemetry` (per-plugin); H `hub:device`
- collector · server · Complex · device logs on the computer: one JSONL file per phone log (each line with `rx`, a reconnect appends), adb reverse every 2 s, heat and system frames every `everyS` while device mode is on (matched by model and app id), a wired phone's `telemetry` lines while it records, the computer mark route `{path}/perf/mark`; idle on a dev server; houses the runtime-free `collector/report` (parse, summary per screen and rate, compare, text) · `sessions`, `mark`, `adb`, `settled` · E `collector:session` (per-plugin); H `hub:device`, `connect:telemetry`
- pages · server · Complex · serves the prebuilt tools page with the boot JSON, `/assets/*`, `/hello` and `/hmr`; home of the `moku-editor` bin (Bun hot reload on, switched by restarting its server, D-32; `--no-hmr` starts it off), the `.moku/editor.json` discovery file, the stdio MCP bridge (`mcp/`) and the perf CLI (`perf/`: `perf`, `perf mark`, `perf summary`, `perf compare`); depends on collector · `routes`, `attachServer`, `hotReload`, `setHotReload`, `attachPerf` · H `collector:session`

### Tools core (`editor-tools`)

- link · tools · Complex · the tools page's only connection: boot JSON, socket, session choice, remote EditorChannel, files client, link status, taps and heap; a -32008 watch is not logged or retried · `read`, `watch`, `run`, `status`, `manifest`, `onManifest`, `sessions`, `session`, `choose`, `retry`, `boot`, `frameUrl`, `isOtherTab`, `onTap`, `heap`, `files`, `hotReload`, `onHotReload`, `setHotReload`, `selection`, `notify`, `handle` (the editor page role: publishes the selection, answers `editor.select`), `project`, `engine`, `onEngine`, and the policy-free seams of the device source: `published`, `onPublished`, `onSessions`, `onHeartbeat`, `ownSession`, `runIn`, `callEditor` · E `link:status`, `link:project`
- activeSource · tools · Standard · one source per tools page (the local preview, a phone or another page): pauses the local preview while a phone is the source and resumes it after, follows phones that link and leave (notice, markers, a rejoin within 15 s), holds connect's scan and watch leases, the connection bar's health and a phone's clock offset · `current`, `preview`, `useDevice`, `useLocal`, `onChange`, `directory`, `scan`, `connectWire`, `connectNetwork`, `connectDevice`, `confirmPairing`, `refusePairing`, `stopDevices`, `telemetry`, `onTelemetry`, `markers`, `notice`, `dismissNotice`, `reconnect`, `label`, `health`, `clockOffsetMs`, `openConnect` · E `activeSource:changed`, `activeSource:connect-requested` (per-plugin); H `link:status`
- workspace · tools · Complex · the shell: top bar with the game mark (compact with a ⋯ menu below 900 px), rail (Game first and default), palette, toasts, keys, Esc unwinding, prefs (theme, density, preview, device and fold, Show taps, sound, Copy on select), twenty-one device presets (default iPhone 18 Pro), the compact bar's Hot reload icon, one game iframe with a playable pinned preview, tap ripples, D-07 reload and Bun hot reload, overlay-in-game and Hot reload switches, the computer's engine in the top bar, the source pill and its menu, the disconnect notice, the paused veil over the local frame, the scenario picker (dev only) · `startLocalPreview`, `scenarios`, `setScenario`, `show`, `density`, `setDensity`, `copyOnSelect`, `setCopyOnSelect`, `device`, `setDevice`, `devices`, `gameFrame`, `palette`, `toast`, `keys`, `mount`, `host`, `badge`, `setOverlayInGame`, `hotReload`, `setHotReload` · E `workspace:changed`, `workspace:ran`, `workspace:density`; H `link:status`, `activeSource:changed`
- panels · tools · Standard · panel host for `definePanel` specs; holds `shared/` view modules (scene, style edit, highlight, `SidePanel`) · `register`, `run`, `list`, `mountInto` · E `workspace:ran`; H `link:status`, `workspace:changed`
- flowView · tools · VeryComplex · Flow workspace: flow-graph canvas with ELK (spacing by density, labels never overlap), focus, Info-tab neighbours with followEdge (frames both ends, pulse), Find current, trail, an item holding the current node is never dimmed and says "here", the Inspector with its Info and Code tabs · `camera`, `focus`, `flows`, `layout` · E `workspace:open-file`; H `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:changed`, `workspace:select-node`, `workspace:focus-frame`, `workspace:density`
- gameView · tools · Complex · Game workspace (the default): device stage (grouped presets, one Fit scale per kind, modern and home-button frames, Fold/Unfold), Sound and Copy Ref switches, picker (the Select icon button), style card, Code section, Styles fields with pending style edits for the agent, area drags, a pick that bookmarks, saves two JPEGs, writes the card file and copies one line, the selection published to MCP and answered `editor.select`, screenshots, series, compact capture card, contact sheet (on request); no scene read from a phone · `pick`, `inspect`, `scene`, `locate`, `highlight`, `capture`, `series`, `stopSeries`, `openSheet`, `copyReference`, `fold`, `bookmarks`, `editStyle`, `clearEdits`, `edits`, `copyEdits` · E `workspace:reveal`, `workspace:open-file`; H `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:changed`, `workspace:open-sheet`, `workspace:inspect`
- renderView · tools · Complex · Render workspace, Mission control, of the page's one source: connection bar with the Connect panel (By wire, On the network, Linked devices), a 2-minute frame timeline with GC, shader and pass lanes, range selection and inspector, cards (FPS with the rate switch, frame time, draws, textures, GPU passes, memory from CDP for a wired phone, device load), Record, Monitoring, Scene details (render tree, textures, bundles, pools, release log; never read from a phone) · `mission`, `inspect`, `pause`, `live`, `setSpan`, `seek`, `select`, `step`, `jump`, `setRate`, `setSection`, `setOverdraw`, `record`, `mark`, `refresh`, `snapshot`, `reveal`, `highlight`, `sortTextures`, `filterBundle` · E `workspace:inspect`, `workspace:open-file`; H `workspace:changed`, `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:reveal`, `activeSource:changed`, `activeSource:connect-requested`
- stateView · tools · Standard · State workspace: player/session trees, last commit derived by diffing `game.model`, runner card · `lastCommit`, `note`, `onCommit`, `tainted`, `graph`, `expanded`, `setExpanded`, `expandAll` · H `link:status`, `workspace:ran`
- filesView · tools · Complex · Files workspace: tree, tabs, viewer, editor, previews, conflict bar, Used by · `open`, `close`, `save`, `resolveConflict`, `refresh`, `fileOf`, `flowFileOf`, `usedBy`, `editorUrl`, `subscribe` · E `workspace:select-node`, `workspace:open-sheet`; H `link:status`, `link:project`, `workspace:changed`, `workspace:open-file`
- consoleView · tools · Standard · Console workspace: `game.log` table, level filter, search, Preserve log, command errors, rail badge · `lines`, `visible`, `counts`, `setFilter`, `clear`, `setPreserve`, `refresh`, `focusFrame`, `subscribe` · E `workspace:focus-frame`; H `link:status`, `workspace:ran`

## Dependency graph and init order

```
agent:  registry → channel → perf → recorder → overlay   (bridge, capture opt-in, after every default)
        channel  depends [registry]
        perf     depends [registry]
        recorder depends [registry, perf]
        overlay  depends [registry, channel, perf, recorder]
        bridge   depends [registry, channel, recorder]
        capture  depends [registry]
server: files → hub → connect → collector → pages   (connect depends [hub]; collector depends [files, hub, connect]; pages depends [files, hub, collector])
tools:  link → activeSource → workspace → panels → flowView, gameView, renderView, stateView, filesView, consoleView
        activeSource depends [link]; workspace depends [link, activeSource]
        every view depends [link, panels]; all but stateView also [workspace]; renderView also [activeSource]
```

## Wire

- Socket URL: `{path}/ws?token=<t>&kind=agent|tools` (default path `/__editor`). Hello: `GET {path}/hello` → `{ ws, token }`.
- Device role (device listener, `moku-editor perf`): `{path}/ws?kind=agent&role=device[&device=<id>&token=<token>]`, the WebView's Origin in `deviceOrigins`, no hub token. Without credentials the first message is `editor` `pair { code, device: { model?, os?, engine?, build?, appId? } }` (four digits; a LAN phone is confirmed by the person, an adb phone under `pairing: "lan"` at once) → `paired { device, token, engine }`; then `hello` as any agent. `perf.lines { log, from, lines }` (lines as JSON objects, 1–5000) → `perf.ack { log, next, n }`. A stale device token: close 4401 `unpaired` after the open (the bridge pairs again). A device session carries `SessionInfo.device` `{ id, model, link, address, port, engine, build, appId? }`; the hub pings each phone once a second (`LinkedDevice.latencyMs`).
- Agent → hub: `hello { manifest, caps? }` (first, else close 1008; `caps: ["run-from"]` asks for stamped runs), `heartbeat`, `value { sub, value }`, `tap { x, y, at }`, `bye`.
- Hub → agent: requests `manifest`, `read`, `watch`, `unwatch`, `run` (channel `game`; to a `run-from` agent a run is `{ id, input?, from: "page" | "mcp", client? }`); notification `session` (channel `editor`).
- Tools → hub: `game` channel `manifest`, `read`, `run`, `watch`, `unwatch`; `files` channel `list`, `read`, `write`, `writeBinary`, `readBinary`, `find { key }`; `editor` channel connect's methods `connect.scan`, `connect.wire`, `connect.network`, `connect.off { lan? }`, `connect.confirm { ticket, code }`, `connect.refuse { ticket }`, `connect.watch { device }`, `connect.unwatch { device }` (tools sockets only), and the MCP bridge's notification `client { name }`.
- Hub → tools: `sessions { list }` (each `SessionInfo` with `heartbeat { frame, paused, silent }` once known and `manifestHash`, the `commandsHash` of its commands, set on hello; re-sent when paused or silent flips), `session`, `hotReload { hmr, owner }`, `project` (the `ProjectState`, kept and replayed; channel `editor`), `engine` (`EngineInfo` `{ id, version, dist, patch? }`, kept and replayed), `devices` (`DeviceDirectory`) and `deviceTelemetry` (`DeviceTelemetry`, 1 Hz), both connect's, kept and replayed, forwarded `heartbeat`, `value` and `tap`.
- Long calls: a `run` of `editor.series` waits `durationMs`, a `run` of `editor.sheet` `frames × everyMs`, on top of the call deadline (capped at +60 s) in bridge, hub and link.
- Error codes: -32600 invalid request, -32601 unknown method/id, -32602 invalid input, -32000 command failed, -32001 game reloaded (retryable), -32002 timeout / link closed (retryable), -32003 no session / choose session, -32004 forbidden path, -32005 version conflict, -32006 not JSON, -32007 unauthorized, -32008 not installed (the game does not have the source), -32009 `read_only` (the page's build refuses the command: `--debug=read`, or `--debug` of engine 0.15.0) or `dev_only` (a page with neither the dev nor the debug flag). connect: -32000 `port_in_use` / `no_lan`, -32007 `not_owner`, -32602 `no_ticket`. Every message starts with `[moku-editor] `.

## MCP for Claude Code

- Setup in the game folder: `claude mcp add moku-editor -- bunx moku-editor mcp web/index.html --port 3000`, or a `.mcp.json` with `{ "mcpServers": { "moku-editor": { "type": "stdio", "command": "bunx", "args": ["moku-editor", "mcp", "web/index.html", "--port", "3000"] } } }` (`moku-editor mcp-config` prints it). `claude mcp list` then shows `moku-editor … ✔ Connected`. Add `.moku/` to the game's `.gitignore`.
- The bridge (`src/plugins/pages/mcp/`) is a separate process and a hub tools client. Newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio; stdout carries only protocol frames. Protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`. Claude Code 2.1.280 probes `server/discover` first (answered -32601), then sends `initialize` 2025-11-25 (fixtures in `src/plugins/pages/__tests__/fixtures/`).
- Which editor: a live `<root>/.moku/editor.json` (`{ version, pid, port, url, ws, token, root, html, startedAt }`, 0600, written by the bin, removed on stop) wins; otherwise the bridge starts `moku-editor <html> --port <port> --root <root>` itself (log `.moku/editor.log`) and owns it; with no html known, in a moku-game folder (`index.ts` + `config.ts`), it starts the engine form `moku-editor --port <port> --root <root>` (D-63), at startup and on `moku_start {}`. On stdin end, SIGINT or SIGTERM it aborts pending calls, closes the socket and stops only a bin it started; exit 0.
- Generic tools (22): `moku_status`, `moku_sessions` (with `heartbeat` and `manifestHash`), `moku_manifest`, `moku_read`, `moku_wait`, `moku_run`, `moku_screenshot` (`editor.capture`, JPEG by default, max width 1080, `key` crops to one ui element; over 300 KB taken once more at half width), `moku_series` (`editor.sheet` at 1080 px wide as JPEG, or `game.capture { sheet }` for an agent without it; game ≥ 0.4), `moku_reference` (the newest or a named card of `.moku/captures/<yyyy-mm-dd>/`, newest day first, and of the older flat `.moku/captures/`), `moku_selection` (the editor page's `SelectionInfo` and its crop; its `edits` are the pending style edits of the element, `{ path, from, to }`, to apply in the source), `moku_select` (exactly one of `{ key }`, `{ rect }` or `{ node }`: `key` and `rect` are relayed to the editor page, which picks it; the selection with its card and crop. `node` selects a node of the flow graph: `editor.show { workspace: "flow" }`, `editor.node { id }`, then `files.find { key: "node:<id>" }`; `{ id, selected, places }`, no card), `moku_device` (`{ preset?, orientation?, folded? }` → hub `editor.device`; `DeviceInfo` with the viewport `w`, `h` and the presets; `{}` reads), `moku_show` (`{ workspace? }` → hub `editor.show`; `{ workspace, workspaces }`), `moku_files_list`, `moku_files_read`, `moku_files_write`, `moku_files_find` (`{ key }` → hub `files.find`; the places `{ path, binding?, line, hash, broken? }`; index off: `isError` "project index off: <reason>"), `moku_project` (`{ path?, prefix? }`, at most one: the project index the hub published; a summary with the key count per prefix, the keys of a prefix with their def paths, or `{ defines, uses, broken? }` of a file; `jsx:` keys are not in it), `moku_reload`, `moku_hot_reload` (`{ on }`: `POST P/hmr` with the discovery token, then waits at most 15 s for the bin's restart; `{ hmr, owner, restarted }`; a game's own server is `isError`), `moku_start`, `moku_stop`. The editor requests `device`, `show` and `node` are relayed to the editor page like `select` (D-60): no page open is -32003 `no_editor_page` with the URL, a bin or a page older than the bridge (-32601, from the hub or from the page) reads "moku-editor or its editor page is older than the bridge; restart moku-editor and reload the page". `.moku/editor.json` and `.moku/editor.log` are hidden from and refused by the file tools; the token is in no tool result.
- Door tools (D-35, D-36, D-37): after the 22 generic tools, `tools/list` holds one tool per command door of the selected session (the one `moku_run` uses without `session`: the only one, else the embedded one; several and none embedded: none). Name: the id with `.` as `_` (`game.tap` → `game_tap`); cheat and raw doors carry the effect first (`cheat_game_fill`, `raw_game_restore`). Typed input schema per door field, optional `_session`; the answer reads like `moku_run`. No tool for the doors the generic tools cover (`game.capture`, `editor.capture`, `editor.sheet`, `editor.series`, `editor.seriesStop`, `editor.reload`; screenshots go only through `moku_screenshot`, JPEG by default, about 300 KB at most), a name starting with `moku_` or longer than 40, an id outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, a field `_session` or outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}`, two doors of one name; each is logged once on stderr and `moku_run` still runs it. The hub stamps `SessionInfo.manifestHash` (`commandsHash` of the session's commands); the bridge rebuilds the door tools and sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` only when that hash moves (an 8 s grace keeps the set while no session is chosen or the hub socket is closed, so a hot reload of the same game and the bin's restart change nothing; after a closed socket the bridge reconnects at the close and 1, 3 and 7 s after it while the bin lives). The first `tools/list` waits at most 3 s for them. `initialize` carries `instructions` on generic versus door tools and on the tools that drive the editor itself. Deny the cheat and raw doors with `{ "permissions": { "deny": ["mcp__moku-editor__cheat_*", "mcp__moku-editor__raw_*"] } }`. A client that does not refresh after `list_changed` keeps the old list; a gone door answers `isError`, and `moku_run` runs every door.
- Who ran it: `initialize` hands the MCP client's name (`clientInfo.title`, else `clientInfo.name`) to the hub as `client { name }`; the hub stamps it on the bridge's runs, so `editor.record` from an agent (the door tool `editor_record`, or `moku_run`) reads `startedBy: { by: "agent", name: "Claude Code" }`.
- Pictures need the game page visible: a paused or hidden game answers `isError` "game paused or hidden at frame N — bring the editor pane to front or resume".

## File structure

```
src/
  config.ts          three createCoreConfig calls, AgentEvents/ServerEvents/ToolsEvents, createAgentPlugin/createServerPlugin/createToolsPlugin
  index.ts           package root: protocol types and helpers, definePanel
  agent.ts           @moku-labs/editor/agent
  agent-page.ts      @moku-labs/editor/agent/page (default export: the engine's PageAgent)
  server.ts          @moku-labs/editor/server
  tools.ts           @moku-labs/editor/tools
  plugins/
    index.ts         barrel of all 22 instances and type namespaces (imported by no entry)
    registry/        + protocol/ (types, errors, check, wire-value, messages, project, devices, overlay-host, build, hash)
    channel/ bridge/ capture/
    perf/            + feeds/ (Mission control on the agent) + protocol/ (runtime-free: engine types, causes, rate, window and its wire form, values, guards, frames, timeline, passes, sections, memory, gpu, history) + graph/ (the canvas-2D frame graph painter)
    recorder/        + protocol.ts (types only: RecordOrigin, RecorderSource, …) + store/ (OPFS and memory)
    overlay/         place/ model/ paint/ fonts/ (three subset Barlow woff2 faces, OFL.txt) styles/ view/
    files/ hub/ pages/   (hub: protocol/ = the runtime-free device link and tools link; pages: page/ = the tools page source, bin.ts + cli.ts = moku-editor, engine-page.ts = the engine page, mcp/ = the stdio MCP bridge, perf/ = the perf CLI)
    connect/         wire/ (adb allowlist, runner, scan) pairing/ cdp/ telemetry/ protocol/ (runtime-free: DeviceDirectory, DeviceTelemetry, guards)
    collector/       session/ adb/ report/ (runtime-free: parse, summary, compare, text)
    link/ activeSource/ workspace/ (styles/ = shared CSS layer) panels/ (shared/ = view modules, icons, workspaces)
    flowView/ gameView/ stateView/ filesView/ consoleView/
    renderView/      source/ series/ view/ timeline/ (painters, paint loop) derive/ actions/ components/ (Mission control and the scene cards)
    <name>/__tests__/unit, __tests__/integration
tests/
  unit/              framework-level unit tests
  integration/       root stack tests (helpers/stack.ts: startStack, shutdown); tiny game in CI, merge-game locally;
                     agent-bundle.test.ts (needs `bun run build`), not-installed.test.ts, mcp-bridge.test.ts (bin + bridge processes),
                     agent-page.test.ts, tree-bundle.test.ts (tsdown once when dist/agent-page.mjs is missing)
  fixtures/          tiny-screen-game.tsx; moku-game.ts (a moku-game folder for the engine page tests)
scripts/build-tools.ts   bundles the tools page into dist/tools (fonts from workspace/styles/fonts and overlay/fonts)
scripts/overlay-fonts.ts subsets the overlay's Barlow faces (bun run fonts:overlay)
scripts/tree/bundle.ts   the editor tree's serve plugin for the engine page (D-50); repo only, not in the package
```

## Scripts

`bun run build` (tsdown + build:tools) · `bun run build:tools` · `bun run fonts:overlay` · `bun run typecheck` · `bun run test` · `bun run test:unit` · `bun run test:integration` · `bun run test:coverage` · `bun run test:e2e` (Playwright: four Chromium windows 480–1440 px; e2e/edit-loop.spec.ts prints save → frame ms per edit) · `bun run lint` · `bun run lint:fix` · `bun run format` · `bun run validate`

## Docs

- README.md: overview, quick start, use with Claude Code (MCP), production builds, plugins, configuration, events
- llms-full.txt: verbatim Config/Api/Event types, config reference, examples, error codes, custom plugins
- src/plugins/<name>/README.md: per-plugin detail
- Moku Core specification: https://github.com/moku-labs/core/tree/main/specification
